answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock scarce collateral in a public registry before it may bid for work. When an agent is caught claiming multiple identities to capture a reward, the protocol slashes those bonds and distributes the loss to honest participants. This makes a sybil attack costly in proportion to the number of identities: the attacker must buy and immobilize more collateral, while risking forfeiture for each. A meadow marketplace, a narrow inlet, or a distant horizon does not change that accounting; geography cannot make duplicate identities free.
